title: Deploy sweep: health validator for VPC API + model priming
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Objective: implement a 'deploy sweep' validator that runs immediately after a VPC/private deployment or upgrade and verifies API readiness, model loadability, and a lightweight load/smoke pass. The sweep should be fast (ideally < 6 minutes end-to-end for a single zone) and deterministic so on-call and automation can make rollout decisions. Scope covers Terraform hooks, an orchestrator Lambda/agent that executes probes, and result reporting into Console and the deployment pipeline.

Why this ticket: existing checks are fragmented across scripts and have inconsistent signal for rollbacks. We need a consolidated, opinionated sequence that covers control-plane handshake, TLS/certs, model runner readiness, KV cache warmup verification, and a small but representative inference sample to catch regressions.

Decision notes and trade-offs:
- We intentionally favor a short sequence of well-chosen checks over long soak tests in this sweep. Longer soak/load tests will remain a separate pipeline triggered by successful sweeps.
- Use existing Terraform module hooks (post_apply) to trigger the sweep; we avoid adding blocking behavior to Terraform apply to keep deployments fast. Instead, the apply will mark a 'verification required' tag and the sweep agent retries until completion or timeout.
- For model priming we will run 1-2 representative prompts per model family rather than exhaustive prompt sets to limit token cost and time.

Operational expectations:
- Sweep returns structured verdict: PASS / WARN / FAIL. FAIL should auto-open an incident playbook and annotate the deployment. WARN should surface to Console as degraded but not block automated rollbacks.

Instrumentation: capture per-step timings, p95 latency for inference sample, success rate for control-plane API handshakes, and model load times (cold load + KV cache priming time). Results stored to an S3 bucket and indexed in Console under deployment events.
acceptance_criteria: Sweep can be triggered via Terraform post-apply hook and also on-demand from Console
Control-plane API handshake: GET /health returns 200 and TLS chain validated within 10s
Model runner reports READY and model artifact hash matches pinned version
Run a representative inference for each pinned model variant with p95 latency < 750ms and 99% exact-success (no errors)
KV cache warmup: after priming prompts, subsequent token-generation requests show decreased latency and cache-hit metric increments
Sweep reports aggregated verdict to Console and writes raw artifacts to s3://redwood-deploy-verifications/<deployment-id>/
On FAIL, the sweep triggers the configured incident webhook and attaches log bundle and minimal reproduction inputs
Automated retry policy: sweep retries up to 3 times with exponential backoff; final state recorded
Tests included in CI: unit tests for sweep controller and an integration test that runs against a small dev VPC stack
Documentation: runbook in Confluence and a short Console UI flow for manual reruns
tasks: Design sweep state machine (stages: control-plane, networking, model-load, inference-smoke, reporting)
Add Terraform module hook that tags deployment id and queues sweep job to orchestration service
Implement sweep orchestration lambda/agent with retries, timeout, and structured events
Create model priming library mapping pinned models -> representative prompts
Instrument metrics (timings, p95 latency, cache-hit delta) and send to telemetry pipeline
Wire reporting: write raw artifacts to S3 and push summary to Console deployment events UI
Add feature flag to enable/disable sweep per-tenant for initial rollout
E2E integration test: deploy minimal VPC stack in staging, run sweep, assert PASS
Author Confluence runbook and Console help text
